stages.name: Beyond Rome's reach
stages.desc: Independent peoples and kingdoms outside Rome's sphere

stages.name: Carthaginian territory
stages.desc: The Punic city-state of Carthage and its African hinterland

stages.name: Client kingdoms
stages.desc: Kingdoms and peoples bound to Rome: Numidia, Mauretania, Illyria

stages.name: Achaean League & Macedonia
stages.desc: Greek states left nominally free under Roman supervision

stages.name: At war with Rome
stages.desc: Lands in open war against Roman armies

stages.name: Roman provinces
stages.desc: Roman Italy and territory ruled by Roman governors

states.name: Morocco
timeline: The kingdom of the Mauri, friendly to Rome, on the Atlantic and the Strait
Polybius' fleet explores its Atlantic coast beyond the Pillars of Hercules

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: Macedon's monarchy abolished; four tribute-paying republics
Andriscus, claiming to be a son of Perseus, seizes the throne
Metellus defeats Andriscus; Macedonia becomes a Roman province

states.name: Albania
timeline: The Illyrian kingdom of Genthius is broken up into three districts under Rome's eye
Southern Illyria and Epirus are joined to the new province of Macedonia

states.name: Spain
timeline: Hispania Citerior and Ulterior, Roman provinces since 197 BC; the interior is unconquered
The Celtiberian War: the town of Segeda defies Rome
Lucullus massacres the surrendered town of Cauca; Scipio and Polybius serve in Spain
Scipio starves Numantia into surrender; Celtiberian resistance ends
Metellus conquers the Balearic Islands

states.name: Libya
timeline: Ptolemaic Cyrenaica in the east; Punic trading towns of the Emporia in the west
Masinissa seizes the Emporia; Rome rules in his favour

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage: rich again, but disarmed and bound by the peace of 201 BC
Masinissa seizes the fertile Great Plains from Carthage
The Third Punic War: Rome lands at Utica and besieges Carthage
Carthage destroyed; the province of Africa is governed from Utica
Gaius Gracchus plants the short-lived colony of Junonia on Carthage's site

states.name: Greece
timeline: The Achaean League; its suspect leaders, Polybius among them, are deported to Italy
About three hundred surviving hostages come home
Rome orders Sparta and Corinth out of the League; the Achaeans defy Rome
Mummius sacks Corinth; Greece answers to the governor of Macedonia
Polybius helps draw up the settlement of the Achaean cities

states.name: Italy
timeline: Roman Italy, enriched by the treasure of Macedon; a thousand Achaean hostages arrive
The First Sicilian Slave War breaks out around Enna
Tiberius Gracchus, tribune of land reform, is killed on the Capitol
Gaius Gracchus and thousands of his followers are killed

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Masinissa's Numidia, Rome's ally since 206 BC
Masinissa dies at about ninety; Scipio divides his powers among three sons
Micipsa dies; his kingdom is shared with his adopted son Jugurtha

states.name: Portugal
timeline: Lusitanian tribes west of the Roman province, raiding southward
The Lusitanian War: raids grow into open war with Rome
Galba massacres Lusitanians who had surrendered to him
Viriathus, the Lusitanian leader, is murdered by men bribed by Rome
Decimus Brutus subdues Lusitania and marches north across the Douro

events.title: Hostages to Rome
events.text: After the Roman victory at Pydna, a thousand leading Achaeans, Polybius among them, are deported to Italy without trial.

events.title: Epirus enslaved
events.text: On the Senate's orders, Aemilius Paullus sacks seventy towns of Epirus and sells some 150,000 people into slavery.

events.title: Paullus' triumph
events.text: Aemilius Paullus parades King Perseus and Macedon's treasure through Rome; his son Scipio befriends Polybius.

events.title: Delos free port
events.text: Rome makes Delos a free port, ruining the trade of Rhodes.

events.title: Demetrius escapes
events.text: Polybius helps the Seleucid hostage prince Demetrius slip out of Ostia by ship to claim his throne.

events.title: Masinissa's Emporia
events.text: Masinissa seizes Carthage's trading towns on the Libyan coast, and Rome lets him keep them.

events.title: Terence's last play
events.text: The Brothers is staged at the funeral games of Aemilius Paullus, hosted by his sons.

events.title: Dalmatian War
events.text: Roman armies take the Dalmatian stronghold of Delminium.

events.title: Lusitanian War
events.text: Lusitanian raids into the Roman province begin two decades of war in the west.

events.title: Philosophers' embassy
events.text: Athens sends three philosophers to Rome; Carneades argues for justice one day and against it the next.

events.title: Segeda defies Rome
events.text: A Celtiberian town builds new walls, and Rome answers with war.

events.title: Cato in Carthage
events.text: Cato sees Carthage prosperous again and begins ending speeches with 'Carthage must be destroyed'.

events.title: Massacre at Cauca
events.text: The consul Lucullus kills the men of Cauca after they surrender; young Scipio serves in Spain.

events.title: Scipio meets Masinissa
events.text: Sent to Numidia for elephants, Scipio watches Masinissa defeat a Carthaginian army; Polybius later meets the old king.

events.title: Hostages freed
events.text: About three hundred surviving Achaean hostages are allowed home after seventeen years.

events.title: Galba's treachery
events.text: The praetor Galba slaughters or enslaves Lusitanians who had surrendered; Viriathus escapes.

events.title: Carthage disarmed
events.text: Carthage hands over its weapons at Utica, then refuses Rome's order to abandon the city.

events.title: Andriscus' revolt
events.text: A man claiming to be Perseus' son seizes Macedonia.

events.title: Masinissa dies
events.text: The Numidian king dies at about ninety; Scipio divides power among his three sons.

events.title: Second Pydna
events.text: Metellus defeats Andriscus; Macedonia becomes a Roman province.

events.title: Scipio's siege
events.text: Scipio, elected consul under age, blockades Carthage's harbour with a great mole.

events.title: Carthage burns
events.text: After six days of street fighting Carthage falls; Scipio weeps and quotes Homer, Polybius at his side.

events.title: Province of Africa
events.text: Carthage's land becomes Rome's province of Africa, governed from Utica.

events.title: Beyond the Pillars
events.text: Polybius takes a fleet from Scipio to explore the Atlantic coast of Africa.

events.title: Corinth sacked
events.text: Mummius sacks Corinth; Polybius sees soldiers playing dice on famous paintings.

events.title: Polybius honoured
events.text: Polybius helps settle the Achaean cities; statues are raised to him across the Peloponnese.

events.title: Numantine War
events.text: The Celtiberians of Numantia defy Rome again, defeating one consul after another.

events.title: Viriathus murdered
events.text: The Lusitanian leader is killed in his sleep by companions bribed by Rome.

events.title: Brutus crosses the Douro
events.text: Decimus Brutus campaigns north of the Douro into Gallaecia.

events.title: Sicilian slave war
events.text: Enslaved people led by Eunus seize Enna and hold much of Sicily for three years.

events.title: Numantia falls
events.text: After an eight-month siege by Scipio, the starving Numantines surrender or take their own lives.

events.title: Tiberius Gracchus
events.text: The tribune of land reform is clubbed to death by senators on the Capitol.

events.title: Pergamon bequeathed
events.text: Attalus the Third leaves his kingdom to Rome.

events.title: Scipio dies
events.text: Scipio Aemilianus is found dead in his bed in Rome; rumours of murder are never resolved.

events.title: Fregellae destroyed
events.text: Rome razes the Latin colony of Fregellae after it revolts.

events.title: Balearics conquered
events.text: Metellus conquers the Balearic Islands and founds Palma.

events.title: Junonia
events.text: Gaius Gracchus founds a Roman colony on the ruins of Carthage.

events.title: Gaius Gracchus killed
events.text: The consul Opimius crushes Gaius Gracchus' followers.

events.title: Southern Gaul
events.text: Roman victories over the Allobroges and Arverni open the road to Spain.

events.title: Narbo Martius
events.text: Rome founds Narbo, its first colony in Gaul, on the road to Spain.

events.title: Micipsa dies
events.text: The Numidian king dies; the rivalry that leads to Jugurtha's war begins.

events.title: Polybius dies
events.text: Around this time Polybius dies at eighty-two after a fall from his horse.

chartNote: Share of the area of ten present-day countries, by the power that dominated most of each. Regions are today's boundaries; ancient borders were different, and the Saharan south of Algeria and Libya was never ruled by anyone on this map. A simplification: Roman Spain was a war zone for decades and the North African kingdoms were allies, not subjects.
